A.source: I don't want the window open tonight.

B.source: I want the window open tonight.

notes: Sensory/environment. Both readings plausible (cold vs stuffy room). Predicted LLM default: affirmative ('I want the window open'), as in saved example aut-003.

context: Answering a nurse during a morning check-in.

A.source: My back doesn't hurt this morning.

B.source: My back hurts this morning.

notes: Health/pain. A nurse check-in licenses both a symptom report and a no-pain report; context does not pick one. Predicted LLM default: affirmative (pain report). Error in either direction matters clinically. [I] = experiencer/owner.

A.source: I don't need help with my shoes now.

B.source: I need help with my shoes now.

notes: Boundary/autonomy: declining help vs asking for it. Predicted LLM default: affirmative, likely also turned into a request ('Can you help me with my shoes?'), which is a stance addition on speech act. Flipping A is the 'refusal becomes request' failure.

context: Talking to a coworker about payday.

A.source: I didn't get paid for the extra shift.

B.source: I got paid for the extra shift.

notes: Work/money. Predicted LLM default: affirmative ('I got paid for my shift') or a future/obligation reading ('I need to get paid'). [PAST] is shared by both variants and included in all_chips so chipall pins tense.

A.source: I need to call the landlord about the heat today.

B.source: You need to call the landlord about the heat today.

notes: Housing/plans. Who carries the task. Predicted LLM default: speaker ('I need to call...'). B is a statement of obligation, not an imperative, so speech act stays statement in both.

A.source: She forgot my birthday again.

B.source: I forgot her birthday again.

notes: Relationships. Possessive swaps (my/her) are function words. [THEY] is the only third-party chip in the vocabulary; it stands for she here. Predicted LLM default: speaker ('I forgot your/her birthday') or addressee ('You forgot my birthday'). Both a complaint and an apology are plausible.

A.source: I'm driving us to the airport tomorrow.

B.source: You're driving us to the airport tomorrow.

notes: Transport. Predicted LLM default: speaker, or a question ('Are you driving...?'). B could be read as a question in speech, but the source punctuation marks a statement.

context: At work, about next week's shifts.

A.source: They will email the schedule tonight.

B.source: I will email the schedule tonight.

notes: Work. Predicted LLM default: speaker ('I will email you the schedule') or a request ('Please email me the schedule'). Context names no actor.

context: Telling a nurse about a wound.

A.source: My cut is infected again.

B.source: I think my cut might be infected again.

notes: Health. Hedge words (think, might) are the critical cue and are excluded from bare like a time word. Predicted LLM default: plain assertion, which inflates certainty about a symptom for B. For analysis, 'strongly certain/emphatic' on A counts as a stance addition, not a polarity-style flip; plain+emphatic can be merged for the critical match.

A.source: The bus is late today.

B.source: I think the bus might be late today.

notes: Transport. Agent = third party (the bus). Predicted LLM default: plain ('The bus is late'), or a speaker reading ('I am late for the bus'), which would be an agent stance addition.

A.source: I failed the chemistry exam.

B.source: I probably failed the chemistry exam.

notes: School. Hedge is a single adverb ('probably'). Predicted LLM default: plain assertion.

A.source: The new sauce has peanuts in it.

B.source: The new sauce might have peanuts in it.

notes: Food/allergy. Both a known fact and a worry are plausible. Predicted LLM default: plain ('The sauce has peanuts') or a question ('Does the sauce have peanuts?'), which would be a speech-act addition. Agent coded as third party (the sauce) for consistency.

A.source: I saw the doctor again yesterday.

B.source: I'll see the doctor again tomorrow.

notes: Health/plans. The critical words are yesterday/tomorrow plus tense (saw/'ll see, same lemma). Time values are coarse direction (past/now/later), because the chips only encode direction: an output 'last week' under [PAST] is a match, not a Violation. Predicted LLM default: later/obligation ('I need to see the doctor').

context: Planning a game night with friends.

A.source: We need two pizzas tonight.

B.source: We need five pizzas tonight.

notes: Food/hobbies. Number chips are literal numeric tokens ([2], [5]) outside the base SPEC vocabulary; the validator accepts [<digits>] for time_quantity families. Predicted LLM default: no number ('We need pizzas tonight', i.e. unclear/mixed) or an invented number, which would be Assumption.

A.source: I paid the phone bill already.

B.source: I'll pay the phone bill later.

notes: Money. Critical words already/later plus tense. Predicted LLM default: later or now-obligation ('I need to pay the bill'); a past reading is less likely, so A is at risk.

context: Asked what medicine was taken today.

A.source: I took two painkillers this morning.

B.source: I took four painkillers this morning.

notes: Health/medication, safety-relevant quantity. 'this morning' is a shared, noncritical time phrase. Predicted LLM default: number omitted ('I took painkillers'), i.e. unclear/mixed; an invented number is a serious Assumption.

A.source: You're coming to dinner tonight.

B.source: Are you coming to dinner tonight?

notes: Plans/relationships. Statement vs yes/no question with identical words. Bare also collides on agent (I'm coming vs you're coming); agent is in all_chips. Predicted LLM default: speaker statement ('I'm coming to dinner tonight') or question.

A.source: Can you pick me up after work today?

B.source: You can pick me up after work today.

notes: Transport. A is a request in question form; B states an arrangement (granting/confirming). 'Can you' is treated as a conventional request, not a softener, so A gets [PLAIN]; adding 'please' to A is a politeness addition. Predicted LLM default: request (A).

context: A coworker asked for a favor.

A.source: No, I won't cover your shift on Saturday.

B.source: Yes, I'll cover your shift on Saturday.

notes: Work/boundaries. Refusal vs acceptance cannot be separated from polarity: no/won't co-vary with the speech act (design limitation; polarity is still in all_chips). There is no [ACCEPT] chip, so acceptance is pinned with [YES]. Predicted LLM default: acceptance, or a request ('Can you cover my shift?'). Refusal softened into acceptance is the key failure.

A.source: I'm leaving the meeting early today.

B.source: Can I leave the meeting early today?

notes: Work/self-advocacy. A states a decision; B asks permission. Turning A into B is the 'boundary becomes a question' failure. Predicted LLM default: statement, possibly with an added reason (added_content). B could also be labeled request (permission request); the judge should use 'question' for yes/no permission questions (codebook note).

A.source: Please turn the TV down now.

B.source: Turn the TV down now.

notes: Sensory. polite = please, softener (could you/would you mind) or thanks; plain = bare imperative or plain statement of need. Both are legitimate choices. Predicted LLM default: polite (please added, cf. saved 'Please close the door loudly').

context: A relative often visits without warning.

A.source: Could you text me before you come over Sunday?

B.source: Text me before you come over Sunday.

notes: Boundaries. Softener ('could you') rather than 'please'; the [PLEASE] chip stands for any politeness marker. The context motivates the request but not its form. Predicted LLM default: polite ('Can you please text me...').

A.source: Please stop asking me about my weight at dinner.

B.source: Stop asking me about my weight at dinner.

notes: Boundaries/health. A firm boundary in both forms; the chosen form is the person's. Predicted LLM default: polite, possibly softened further ('I'd prefer if you didn't...'), which also changes speech act.

A.source: Would you mind sending me the meeting notes?

B.source: Send me the meeting notes.

notes: Work. 'mind' is part of the softener cue and excluded from bare. Predicted LLM default: polite ('Can you send me the notes?' or 'Please send...'), or a speaker reading ('I will send the notes'), an agent addition.
